subject: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great conversation. Quick recap from our side and the proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Key pain points you called out
- Inconsistent latency on large-batch generation for your customer-facing workflows (spikes during peak hours).
- Rising per-token cost as usage on the recommendation engine has grown 3x in the last 6 months.
- Compliance requirement: audit logs and tighter data-retention controls for EU region workloads.

Goals for the next 12 months
- Stabilize p95 latency to <600ms for the recommendation endpoints
- Reduce per-token cost by ~25% via batching + quantization for non-sensitive workloads
- Expand workload to handle document-summarization pilot (private data) and maintain auditability

What we discussed as a path forward
- Renew current contract (monthly committed capacity) for core workloads.
- Pilot Dedicated capacity for recommendation endpoints (1 month canary, then scale).
- Run a cost/quality evaluation on the summarization workload; option to use Private deployment for the pilot if needed for data controls.

Attachments I shared: Acme_Monthly_Usage_202701.pdf (usage + cost breakdown) and Renewal_Proposed_Tiers_2027-02.xlsx (initial pricing tiers and estimated impact).

Proposed next steps
1) I'll loop in Vivek from Finance to surface the renewal pricing and any available credits for the pilot (cc'd).
2) You confirm the timeline for procurement (are you targeting a March PO?).
3) We kick off the Dedicated canary week of Mar 8 - Redwood will run a pre-cutover checklist and a short load test.

If I missed anything from your side, flag it and I'll update. Otherwise, if the above looks right, I'll draft a short mutual-action plan and share the DocuSign link for the renewal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0132

--
Redwood Inference | Making inference predictable and economical

From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and matches our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

- For latency: the 600ms p95 target is acceptable, but can you confirm whether that includes cold-starts across AZs?
- Procurement: we're aiming to have an approved PO by Mar 15; procurement will need the final SOW and an invoice schedule to proceed. (cc: procurement@acme.com)
- Summarization pilot: yes, likely starts with 5k doc/day ingestion for the proof-of-concept. We will need an NDA addendum if we route any PII.

Also - the usage PDF was helpful. I'll take a pass and send back one question on a line item.

Jordan
Jordan Myers
Senior Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
jordan.myers@acme.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap

Jordan - thanks for the quick reply and the clarifying Qs. Responses below inline.

On Thu, Feb 25, 2027 at 12:04 PM Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acme.com> wrote:
> - For latency: the 600ms p95 target is acceptable, but can you confirm whether that includes cold-starts across AZs?

Good question - our SLA targets and the Dedicated canary scope exclude cold-starts due to instance spin-up. For the recommendation endpoints we recommend a warm pool (reserved capacity) to keep cold-starts negligible; the pre-cutover checklist calls for a 10-15 minute warmup and a KV cache priming step. I'll add explicit language to the mutual action plan that the 600ms p95 target assumes the warm pool strategy.

> - Procurement: we're aiming to have an approved PO by Mar 15; procurement will need the final SOW and an invoice schedule to proceed.

Vivek - can you share the SOW template and invoice schedule options we typically provide for Dedicated renewals? Jordan, I'll prepare a one-page SOW for the pilot and a proposed invoice schedule (monthly with an upfront first-month prorated charge) and push both to DocuSign once you confirm.

> - Summarization pilot: yes, likely starts with 5k doc/day ingestion for the proof-of-concept. We will need an NDA addendum if we route any PII.

We can support a Private deployment for the pilot if you need the additional controls; our legal team can produce a two-way addendum covering PII and retention.

Action items
- Marissa: Draft mutual action plan + DocuSign draft (by EOD Mon Feb 29).
- Vivek: Share SOW template and invoice schedule options (by Mon Feb 29).
- Jordan: Confirm PO timeline (target Mar 15) and whether the pilot requires Private deployment or Dedicated with encryption at rest.

I've re-attached the usage report and pricing tiers for convenience.

Thanks - talk soon.

Marissa

Attachments: Acme_Monthly_Usage_202701.pdf, Renewal_Proposed_Tiers_2027-02.xlsx

From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme Corp - Renewal & Expansion Recap

All good - thanks for the details, Marissa and Vivek. Procurement confirms the Mar 15 PO target and they prefer monthly invoicing with a 30-day payment term. They also asked for the SOW and invoice schedule by next Monday.

We're inclined to run the pilot on Dedicated first (encryption at rest + VPC peering), and if we hit any compliance blockers we'll shift to Private. Jordan will confirm final requirement on PII routing by next week.

Please go ahead and send the mutual action plan + DocuSign when ready.

Best,
Jordan
